newsitem.title: CHINA: China B shares end up on selective buying.
newsitem.headline: China B shares end up on selective buying.

text.p: China B share indices in Shanghai and Shenzhen ended up on Friday on selective buying in companies expected to benefit from development of the two cities, brokers said.
Shanghai's B index rose 1.140 points or 1.31 percent to 88.098 on volume of 37.975 million shares worth $22.988 million.
Brokers said institutional buying in Pudong shares pushed the index up, but follow-up buying was limited, indicating further sharp gains will be difficult to achieve.
"Some institutions lifted the prices of shares in which they hold large positions, but follow-up buying was not active with most investors cautious," one broker said.
"The market needs a correction in the short term, though some individual stocks may buck the trend," another broker said.

Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development was the most actively traded and became the star on institutional window-dressing buying, jumping $0.092 or 7.30 percent to $1.352 on volume of 3.4 million shares.
Another Pudong share, Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development, followed on the same factors, ending up $0.050 or 7.14 percent to $0.750 on volume of 1.8 million shares.
The Shenzhen B index rose 0.85 points or 0.49 percent to 176.64 on turnover of HK$144.9 million against Thursday's HK$156.6 million.
Analysts said investors favoured companies based in Shenzhen, which borders Hong Kong, because of strong economic prospects for the area ahead of the British colony's handover on July 1.
"As the Hong Kong handover draws near, people are focusing on companies that may gain from it," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Conglomerate Shenzhen Gintian Co was the best performer, rising HK$0.17 or 4.15 percent to HK$4.27.
China Vanke Co Ltd, also a Shenzhen-based conglomerate, was the second biggest gainer, adding HK$0.34 or 3.84 percent to HK$9.20.
Shanghai's A share index tumbled late in the session on institutional unwinding selling, triggered by talk that Beijing plans to introduce new measures to cool the market, brokers said.

The index slipped 16.925 points or 1.17 percent to 1,426.972 points on volume of 973.1 million shares worth 13.7 billion yuan. The SSE30 blue chip index edged up 1.617 points or 0.04 percent to 3,793.814 points.
The Shenzhen A share index gained 2.34 points or 0.49 percent to close at 483.85 on turnover of 17.8 billion yuan against 14.0 billion yuan on Thursday.
